verdicts.flaw_description: The post-upgrade figures 'cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service' while 'a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed' and are therefore excluded, yet the comparison is to 'the same unit a quarter earlier', which includes all runs. Dropping the bypassed quarter of runs (the ones with no filtration at all) from the treated period alone could produce the 8-14 percent drop.

'Prey abundance on the surrounding farmland ran a third above the previous year's, and every box stood at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range' - a food supply a third larger reaches every plot in the log and on its own explains fledging 9-16 more young than the previous spring, independent of the boxes.

The reported germination 'rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat', while 'about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed' and are left out, but the baseline is the whole previous sowing. The 6-11 point gain is measured on a filtered best-coated subset against an unfiltered comparison.

'Pass rates cover the students who attended every block' while 'about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block' and are excluded, yet the comparison is the previous spring term's full cohort. Restricting to the fully attending three-quarters is enough to raise the measured pass rate by the 4-8 points reported, with no effect from the tutoring itself.
